reason: The cited evidence (E2) directly demonstrates the application of a 120 μm Hf coating on VZrHfNbTa, the formation of a dense HfO₂ layer, and a much lower weight gain versus uncoated samples, supporting all key premises. E1 provides only general background on oxidation challenges in RHEAs and does not directly support the specific intervention.
premises: A Hf-rich coating can be applied to a VZrHfNbTa-based RHEA with a thickness of ~120 μm
During high-temperature oxidation, the Hf coating forms a dense, protective HfO₂ layer
The HfO₂ layer significantly reduces oxidation weight gain compared to an uncoated alloy
The coating prevents surface degradation such as pulverization or spallation
